title: Polynomial threshold sets with large Gaussian surface area
statement: For every natural number $k$ and every real $\varepsilon>0$, there is a real polynomial $p$ in one variable of degree at most $k$ such that the Gaussian surface area of the set $\{x\in\mathbb R:p(x)\ge 0\}$ is at least $\max\!\left(\frac{k}{\sqrt{2\pi}}-\varepsilon,0\right)$.
